description: Starting from Zero, rising beyond Gravity. We are ZeroGravity — a team with no limits to curiosity, creativity, and discovery. summary:
Infinite Nebula, developed by Team ZeroGravity, is an interactive space adventure game that transforms planetary science into an exciting learning experience. Inspired by the concept of Earth analog sites, our project explores how locations on Earth share environmental and geological similarities with regions on Mars.The journey begins when an astronaut-scientist crash-lands on Mars after a radiation burst damages his spacecraft. Stranded far from Earth, he meets a friendly alien who offers spaceship parts in exchange for knowledge about Earth. Players take the astronaut's role and explore five real Martian regions: Jezero Crater, Bagnold Dunes, Eberswalde Crater, Terra Sirenum, and Ares Vallis.Players investigate each region using scientific information and measurements such as temperature, wind, and terrain. They then compare these characteristics with three possible Earth locations and identify the closest match. The game explains why a particular location is a better match and highlights the differences between Earth and Mars. Every successful comparison earns a spaceship part, and collecting all five parts completes the mission. With three levels of exploration, scientific comparisons, and an engaging storyline, Infinite Nebula encourages players to explore, think critically, and discover like planetary scientists. Our vision is to make space science more accessible, interactive, and inspiring.
Infinite Nebula turns scientific curiosity into an adventure of discovery.
details:
How We Addressed the Challenge

We used NASA data to identify and compare common features and differences between Earth and Mars locations, supported by our Kaveri Delta (Earth) – Jezero Crater (Mars) research report. We transformed these scientific findings into INFINITE NEBULA, an interactive game that makes planetary exploration engaging and understandable for everyone.

How We Developed 0ur Project

Every great mission begins with an idea. Ours began with one question: What if exploring Mars could help us understand Earth better?

With this thought, we started building Infinite Nebula — a space adventure that brings scientific discovery into gameplay.

We began by shaping the astronaut's journey into a story. Instead of presenting overwhelming masses of raw scientific data like a dry textbook, we wanted players to discover it through exploration, challenges, and decisions

Next came the science. We explored five regions of Mars and researched Earth locations that share similar environmental and geological characteristics. We collected and checked relevant measurements, then organized them into comparisons that players could understand and use.

But research alone was not enough. We wanted players to experience the discovery. So, we developed a gameplay system where each Martian region presents a new challenge. Players compare three Earth locations, choose the closest match, and discover why their choice is scientifically suitable — including where the comparison is not perfect.

We brought these ideas together through an interactive comic introduction, Mars exploration, Earth–Mars location matching, and a five-part spaceship repair mission. We also planned three difficulty levels to take players from familiar locations to lesser-known planetary analogues.

Game

One of the most exciting features of our game is its diamond-powered environmental scanning system. Diamonds are more than just collectibles. They are the energy source required to activate your environmental scanners. Players must collect the required diamonds before scanning the Martian analogue sites.

And the challenge gets progressively harder! In Easy Mode, players need to collect 5 diamonds. In Moderate Mode, the requirement increases to 10 diamonds. And in Hard Mode, players must collect 15 diamonds. Every difficulty level adds another layer of challenge to the expedition.

Once the scanner is powered, players can proceed with environmental analysis and investigate the similarities between Martian environments and their possible Earth counterparts.

The central scientific idea behind Infinite Nebula is planetary analog research. Our game transforms this scientific concept into an interactive experience, making planetary science more engaging and accessible.

What makes Infinite Nebula special is the way it combines exploration, scientific curiosity and game-based challenges. Instead of simply reading about Mars, players become part of the expedition.

Every scan represents an opportunity to discover something new. Every location brings another scientific question. And every challenge encourages players to think like planetary explorers.

What We Hope to Achieve

  • With Infinite Nebula, we hope to make space science more than something people simply read about. We want it to become something they can explore, experience, and enjoy
  • We also hope to encourage curiosity — especially among young learners — to ask questions, explore unfamiliar places, and see science from a different perspective.
  • In the future, we aim to expand the experience with more planetary regions, lesser-known Earth analog sites, and deeper scientific comparisons. We also hope to make the game more accessible to learners from different backgrounds.
  • Our biggest goal is simple: to turn the distance between Earth and Mars into a connection that anyone can discover.
  • Because sometimes, understanding another world begins by looking more closely at our own.

Impact

- Accessibility: Presents complex scientific ideas through simple explanations, visual comparisons, and an easy-to-follow game experience, helping beginners understand planetary science.

- Engagement: Combines storytelling, exploration, decision-making, and rewards to make learning about Mars more interactive and enjoyable.

- Scientific Awareness: Introduces players to Earth analog sites and helps them understand how scientists compare environmental and geological conditions on Earth with regions of Mars.

- Inspiration: Encourages curiosity about space exploration, scientific research, and the possibilities of future missions to Mars.

Important Note

Although the platform is geared toward children, every feature is grounded in real science. We don’t use fantasy to mislead — instead, we wrap accurate data in narrative so learners can explore safely and meaningfully. The “magic” lies in the game, but the backbone is NASA’s data.

Target Audience

For curious minds of all ages, regardless of age or background — anyone interested in space, science, exploration, and discovering the connection between Earth and Mars.

Scalability: Future Scope

  • More Earth and Mars data : Add more Martian regions and many more Earth analog sites, so players compare a much wider range of places
  • NASA data integration : Connect NASA’s open datasets and APIs so new values can be collected and refreshed from NASA sources, not entered by hand.
  • Other worlds : Extend the game to Europa, Titan, asteroids, and other planets, with each world getting its own set of measured values.
